title: The 51 targets
text: TGT holds the best possible payoff, the target, for each of the 51 tests, read from the test feedback. It sets the scale of each answer.

title: Measured coefficients
text: C has one row per test and 101 Fourier coefficients per row, 5,151 numbers in all. Each one was read off the score of a single probe, so row i describes the hidden curve at t = i / 50.

title: Fourier basis on 100 cells
text: h(k) builds basis vector k on N = 100 equal cells of [0, 1]: a constant for k = 0, then cosines and sines of rising frequency, ending with the alternating vector at k = 100. Each is scaled so the mean of its squares is 1, which is what let one probe measure one coefficient exactly.

title: Rebuild the hidden curve
text: probe(t) picks the row for the nearest t on the 0.02 grid and adds up coefficient times basis vector for every nonzero coefficient. The sum is the hidden curve g, and f = g is the answer with the highest payoff.

title: A branch that never runs
text: None is not None is always false, so these lines do nothing. The script that generated this file left them in.

title: Scale to the target
text: Multiplies by sqrt(2 x target), the unit the coefficients were measured in, so f matches g in size. At f = g the payoff equals the target: a ratio of 1 and full marks.

title: Read t, write the answer
text: Reads one number t from standard input and writes the 100 values, one per line, to the file named by OUTPUT_PATH, where HackerRank collects the output.
